22:The body beneath the tabs has 8 pixels of padding, on the same flat surface as the selected tab, the ribbon's tab row colour, #333333 in dark mode, untinted by the mode, and joined to the selected tab with no line between them. In it, the text input sits in a dark box on the theme's darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, with corners rounded 4 pixels and no border, as tall as the column of buttons beside it, 8 pixels from it, and taller when its text needs more. The text sits 8 pixels in from the box's top, left, and right, and grows down through the box. Clicking anywhere in the box beneath the text puts focus in the text, except while a preview shows. The preview shows in the same box, its content inset 8 pixels all round.
39:<Ctrl+Shift+Enter> (<Cmd+Shift+Enter> on macOS) in the chat input opens the menu with its first option highlighted, and does nothing while the input is empty or a preview shows. While it is open, the text keeps focus, <Up> and <Down> move the highlight, wrapping around, <Enter> picks the highlighted option, and <Escape> closes the menu, as does pressing <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> again or the mouse anywhere outside it. Each option highlights on hover, and clicking one picks it.
62:Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with, at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.
86:To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of help text says what the selected tab is for, and changes as soon as another tab is selected. It is extra small and dimmer than muted text, set a little apart from the last tab, so it reads as a quiet note about the tab rather than as another tab. It is cut off rather than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.
127:The selected tab and the tab body holding the input are not tinted: they stay the flat surface the description gives, whatever the mode, the mode showing in the tab labels' colours and the send button's. The send button's colour transitions smoothly whenever the selected tab changes, straight from the old tab's colour to the new one's. The tabs wrap around, so pressing <Ctrl+Tab> on Freeform fades grey straight to Code's red, and <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> on Code fades red straight to Freeform's grey; neither lights up Chain, Spec, or Ask on the way. A fade to or from Freeform's grey keeps the other tab's hue, only draining or filling its colour, so it never passes through another hue. Between Code and Spec it passes through Chain's colour, whatever colours they have been given in the theme editor.
163:#### Grow To Fit
165:The text input is a [GrowingTextInputScope](../../../ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input-scope) growing to 12 rows at most. Its first row lines up with the send button, both at the top of the input row, and it grows downward from there.
---
## Concept

### Pitch

A multi-line text input that is only as tall as its text, so it takes a single row until there is more to show.

### Shape

#### Description

A multi-line text input whose long lines soft wrap, starting at a single row.

#### Grow To Fit

It grows to fit its text, one row per visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft wrap, wrapped where it wraps them. It shrinks again as text is removed, and fits again when its width changes, as when the window is resized. Its height is what its rows and their padding and border take, and nothing more: there is no empty row beneath the last line.
Its rows are counted as the input itself lays its text out, in the very font it draws the text in, weight and all, so the count never differs from what shows: while the text is within its most rows, no row is ever cut off or scrolled out of view, and no empty row is left. Should a count made ahead of drawing still differ from how the text was laid out, the input takes the laid out count by the next frame.

#### Most Rows

Whatever uses it says how many rows it grows to at most. Once its text takes more, it stays that tall and scrolls.

#### Steadiness

It grows or shrinks in the very frame its text changes, and at any display scale its height is rounded up to a whole device pixel, so the text never flickers a row up and back as a line is added.

cd /home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl; f=spec/ui/components/growing-text-input/index.pi; cat >> $f <<'EOF'

        It never takes its height from a frame before. Its rows are counted
        at the width it is drawn at in this frame, the width its text wraps
        at, so the first line to wrap adds its row in the frame it wraps, at
        its final height, with no frame drawn at the old height with the
        text already wrapped, nor at a height between, nor at a width it
        then wraps again at. Its height is set once a frame, from that count,
        never adjusted after the frame is drawn, so it never settles over
        two or more frames.

        The width its text wraps at never depends on whether it scrolls. Its
        scrollbar, once its text takes more than its most rows, overlays the
        text's right padding rather than taking width from the text, so
        reaching its most rows never rewraps the text, never changes its
        count of rows, and never moves a line from one row to another.

    scrolling:
        Once its text takes more than its most rows, it scrolls only to keep
        the cursor in view, and then by no more than it takes: typing,
        pasting, or moving the cursor to a row beneath the last shown
        scrolls just far enough to show it as the last row, and to a row
        above the first shown, just far enough to show it as the first. A
        change of text, its height, or its width that leaves the cursor in
        view never scrolls it, and a frame never scrolls it to its top and
        back, nor back and forth between two places. Typing at the end of a
        long text keeps its last row the last row shown, steadily, keystroke
        after keystroke. Scrolling it with the wheel or trackpad moves it as
        far as was scrolled and leaves it there until the cursor moves out
        of view. Its scroll position is kept in whole device pixels, so its
        rows never shimmer between two positions.

    nothingElseCapsIt:
        It is as tall as its rows need, up to its most rows, wherever it is
        used: what holds it never caps or fixes its height, nor stretches it,
        but lays itself out around the height the input takes, growing and
        shrinking with it in the same frame. Only its most rows stop it
        growing.
EOF

content.text:
The spec already required growing without jumps, so these are code bugs. I can't see the code from this step, so I tightened the spec around the three likely causes, so the coding step has exact rules to fix them against. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 81 files; the new sections are in the refreshed reference.

**Likely causes:**
- **Jump at the first wrap:** the height is probably worked out at the previous frame's width, then corrected a frame later.
- **Jumping when it gets long:** probably two things together. The scrollbar appears and narrows the text, so it rewraps and the row count changes. The scroll position is also probably reset or chased each frame.
- **Not growing at all:** something around the input, such as the input row, the button column or the tab body, is probably fixing its height.

## What changed in the spec

**1. Growing text input** (`.claude/reference/ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md`)
- **`#steadiness`, two new rules:**
  - Rows are counted at the width the text wraps at in this frame. The height is set once per frame from that count and never adjusted afterwards, so the first wrap lands at its final height with no in-between frame.
  - The scrollbar sits over the right padding instead of taking width from the text. Reaching 12 rows never rewraps the text or changes the row count.
- **`#scrolling` (new):** past its row limit it only scrolls to keep the cursor in view, by the least needed.
  - Typing at the end keeps the last line steadily at the bottom.
  - A change that leaves the cursor visible never scrolls it.
  - It never jumps to the top and back.
  - A wheel or trackpad scroll stays where you put it until the cursor leaves view.
  - The scroll position is kept in whole pixels.
- **`#nothing-else-caps-it` (new):** whatever holds the input never fixes, caps or stretches its height. Only its row limit stops it growing.

**2. Chat input** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#grow-to-fit`)
- The chat input grows from the first wrapped line up to 12 rows, and shrinks back, in the same frame as the text changes.
- The tab body, the input row and the button column never fix its height. The input row is as tall as the text or the buttons, whichever is taller.
- The message list above gives up the room in that same frame.
- The tabs, buttons and session bar never jump while it grows or scrolls.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791137158-Prompt_7b61e528bf74c99f.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `GrowingTextInputScope`: `#grow-to-fit`, `#most-rows`, `#steadiness`, `#scrolling`, `#nothing-else-caps-it`.
- `ChatInputScope`: `#grow-to-fit` and `#description`, for the text box's height against the button column.
